auditor: T2 audit-brainstem (builder) — read-only over src/**; no data file was modified

crossChecked: src/data/tracts.json (23 tracts, incl. tract-mlf, tract-scp, tract-anterior-spinocerebellar)
src/geometry/curves.ts (NERVE_COURSES — the cranial-nerve courses anchored on the exit landmarks and nucleus origin3d)
src/data/syndromes/midbrain.json + hindbrain.json (26 cards) and src/components/viewer3d/NucleusMesh.tsx (how origin3d/size3d are consumed)
scope.geometryMethod: For every record that owns a committed GLB the marker was compared with that mesh's bbox and centroid; for the envelope meshes (ctx-*-surface) and the inferior olive the marker was additionally tested by ray-parity (Moller-Trumbore, unit rays in +x/+y/+z, majority of 3) against the committed triangle soup, and the distance to the nearest surface vertex was measured. Coordinate frame (established from the meshes, not assumed): x = mediolateral (paired records use x>0), y = the levels.json transverse axis (rostral +), z = dorsoventral with DORSAL NEGATIVE (colliculus mesh z -10.4..-5.6, crus cerebri marker z +9, fourth-ventricle mesh z -19.7..-0.7).
constraints: Auditors do not edit data; only the integrator writes corrections.

The committed GLBs and their bboxes are frozen (verify:anatomy 27/27). No finding below asks for a different mesh; where a mesh and an authored field disagree the finding is stated against the authored field, and a conflict that could only be fixed by moving a mesh is filed as unverifiable-here.
size3d is an ellipsoid RADIUS used only as the marker fallback when the record has no GLB (src/types.ts:50, NucleusMesh.tsx:184): size3d << own mesh bbox is by design and is NOT reported.
The browser lane cannot run in this sandbox; no finding here rests on a rendered pixel.

basisKindEnum: internal-contradiction (two authored artifacts disagree: record vs record, record vs plates.json, record vs its own other field)
mesh-contradiction (the record disagrees with its own committed GLB bbox or triangle soup)
textbook (the records' own ref list: Blumenfeld, Patten, Fix, Snell, Nolte)
nomenclature (Terminologia Anatomica / FMA / standard English-Latin usage)
knowledge (this auditor's anatomical knowledge, labelled as such)

counts.note: ok rows carry severity 'minor' because the schema requires a severity for every row; they are verifications, not defects. No 'critical' row was found in the brainstem set: every wrong claim here is a coordinate, a level set or a local text defect, not a wrong localizing sign.

findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's OWN committed GLB: nuc-snc.glb occupies z 7.4..9.4 (y 9.9..11.2, x -9.1..9.0). The authored marker lies at z = 2.5, which is 4.9 au DORSAL of the mesh's most dorsal point and 6.1 au from its centre; even the marker's own z-radius (size3d z = 3.5) only reaches z = 6.0. At 1 au = 1.2 mm the marker is about 6 mm too dorsal, i.e. in the mid-tegmentum next to the red nucleus (nuc-red-nucleus z -2.3..2.4) instead of in the ventral midbrain just dorsal to the crus cerebri, where the substantia nigra actually is.
findings.suggestedFix: Set nuc-snc.origin3d z to about 8.5 (the mesh centroid z is 8.6) and keep x/y; re-check that the point stays inside CLIP_BOUNDS (x[-58,58] y[-55,116] z[-76,72]) — it does.
findings.notes: The mesh is frozen and is not to be moved; this is a finding about the authored marker. For a meshed record origin3d feeds the explode-direction anchor and the selectable fallback (NucleusMesh.tsx:170-184), so the visible effect is the focus/selection anchor sitting in the tegmentum rather than on the nigra.

findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's OWN committed GLB: nuc-snr.glb occupies z 7.9..9.7 (y 8.7..10.2, x -9.1..9.1, centroid z 9.0). The marker sits at z = 3.5, 4.4 au dorsal of the mesh's most dorsal point. nuc-snc (z 2.5, mesh 7.4..9.4) carries the same defect, and the two authored markers keep the correct relative order (SNc dorsal to SNr) while both are displaced ventrally in the real structure's frame — i.e. the pair was placed by hand and never reconciled with the baked nigra.
findings.suggestedFix: Set nuc-snr.origin3d z to about 9.0 (mesh centroid) and, with brainstem-001, keep the SNc/SNr dorsoventral order SNr < SNc that the two meshes already encode.
findings.notes: Same class as brainstem-001; the SNc/SNr split itself (naming, function, connections, Parkinson/saccadic-distractibility clinical) was audited and is correct.

findings.expected: the lateral mid-pons surface, about [15.5, -6, 0] (the record's own derived course exits the pons between its waypoints [13,-6,0] and [16,-5,-2])
findings.basis: Mesh-contradiction with the record's own envelope GLB ctx-pons-surface.glb: the point is INSIDE the pons by ray parity in all three axis directions, 6.66 au from the nearest surface vertex, while the lateral surface at the same level (y = -8, z = 2..4) lies at |x| = 17.3..17.9. The trigeminal root does not leave the pons 10 au (12 mm) medial to its own lateral surface. The record is a `surface` landmark in subdivision `Surface landmarks` named 'Trigeminal nerve (CN V) exit' and the course in src/geometry/curves.ts is anchored on it (waypoint 2 of 7), so the anchor, not only a label, is misplaced.
findings.suggestedFix: Move surf-cn5-exit to the lateral mid-pons surface (about [15.5,-6,0], on the root-exit segment between the course's own waypoints 4 and 5) and re-run the nerve-course recipe (.dsh-swarm/_regen-curves.mjs) so waypoint 2 of nrv-cn5-trigeminal follows; the waypoints stay inside CLIP_BOUNDS.
findings.notes: Cross-file: src/geometry/curves.ts is the integrator's file (plan C2). The sibling landmarks surf-cn6/cn7/cn8-exit were tested the same way and pass (see brainstem-052, -053).

findings.expected: the postolivary sulcus dorsal to the olive, about [6, -34, 0.5]
findings.basis: Mesh-contradiction: the point is INSIDE the inferior olive's own committed GLB nuc-inferior-olive-principal.glb (ray parity 1/1/1 in +x, +y, +z; 0.39 au from the nearest olive surface vertex; the olive's mesh is x +-7.04, y -37.9..-29.9, z 1.0..5.0). Vagal rootlets emerge in the POST-olivary sulcus, dorsal to the olive — in this frame z about 0..1 at x 6 — and not from inside the nucleus. The same point is also 2.9 au inside the medullary envelope. The derived course in curves.ts (waypoints [4,-33,-1] -> [5,-34,4.5]) therefore runs through the olive: the intermediate course point [4.5,-33.5,1.8] is likewise inside the olive mesh (parity 1/1/1).
findings.suggestedFix: Move surf-cn10-exit to about [6,-34,0.5] (postolivary sulcus: at x = 6, y = -34 the points z = 1, 0, -1 are all outside the olive, z = 2 is inside) and re-run the nerve-course recipe so nrv-cn10-vagus waypoint 3 follows.
findings.notes: Cross-file: src/geometry/curves.ts belongs to the integrator (plan C2).

findings.expected: about [6, -31, 0.5] — in the postolivary sulcus, on the same dorsoventral line as the vagal and accessory rootlets
findings.basis: Mesh-contradiction of the same family as brainstem-004: the landmark is 0.42 au from the inferior olive's surface, i.e. resting ON the olive's ventral-anterior face rather than behind it, and the derived course in curves.ts cuts through the olive — the segment from the nucleus [3.5,-31,-4] to the landmark passes through [4.8,-31,2.9], which is inside the olive mesh (parity 1/1/1, 0.85 au from its surface). Internal contradiction with the sibling landmark: surf-cn11-exit sits at z = 2 at the lower medulla (5.3 au clear of the olive), and the preolivary landmark surf-cn12-exit at z = 6.5; z = 4.5 at x = 5 belongs to neither sulcus and falls on the olive itself.
findings.suggestedFix: Move surf-cn9-exit to about [6,-31,0.5] and re-run the nerve-course recipe so nrv-cn9-glossopharyngeal waypoint 2 follows.
findings.notes: Same owner note: the course geometry in src/geometry/curves.ts is the integrator's.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-sensory-decuss", "lvl-olivary", "lvl-pontomedullary"]
findings.expected: the same three plus lvl-pons-caudal, lvl-pons-middle, lvl-pons-rostral, lvl-midbrain-ic and lvl-midbrain-sc
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with plates.json: the atlas's own plate manifests label tract-medial-lemniscus at plate-pons-caudal (lvl-pons-caudal), plate-pons-middle, plate-pons-rostral, plate-midbrain-ic and plate-midbrain-sc — five levels the record says it is not visible at. `levels` is documented as 'level ids where visible' (src/types.ts:48) and drives the InfoPanel level chips, so the record under-claims a tract that the plates draw from the sensory decussation to the midbrain (its own function text already says it 'climbs through pons toward its midbrain position').
findings.suggestedFix: Extend tract-medial-lemniscus.levels to the eight levels its course and the plates actually use: lvl-sensory-decuss, lvl-olivary, lvl-pontomedullary, lvl-pons-caudal, lvl-pons-middle, lvl-pons-rostral, lvl-midbrain-ic, lvl-midbrain-sc.
findings.notes: This was the only plate/levels disagreement in the audit that the plates can settle on the record side; the 5 reverse cases (plate labels a level the record omits) are brainstem-007..011.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-post-comm"]
findings.expected: ["lvl-midbrain-sc", "lvl-post-comm"] (or the plate label moved — see notes)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with plates.json: plate-midbrain-sc (levelId lvl-midbrain-sc) carries the label nuc-pretectal, but the record's levels contain only lvl-post-comm. The record's own committed mesh sits at y 16.0..18.5, i.e. between the two anchors (lvl-midbrain-sc y = 14, lvl-post-comm y = 19) but nearer lvl-post-comm, so the record is right that its centre of mass belongs to the posterior-commissure level and the plate label is at least arguable.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add lvl-midbrain-sc to nuc-pretectal.levels (the rostral pole of the pretectum does reach the superior-colliculus plate) or delete/move the label on plate-midbrain-sc — one of the two, so the plate and the record agree.
findings.notes: Cross-file: the plate side belongs to T5 audit-tracts-plates; this finding is filed against the record field so that the integrator has both options in one ledger row.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-midbrain-sc"]
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with plates.json: plate-midbrain-ic (lvl-midbrain-ic, y = 8) labels tract-crus-cerebri, but the record claims visibility only at lvl-midbrain-sc (y = 14). The crus cerebri is a continuous ventral column through the whole midbrain down to the pontomesencephalic junction, so its presence at the inferior-colliculus level is not in doubt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lvl-midbrain-ic to tract-crus-cerebri.levels.
findings.notes: Cross-file: T5 owns the plate manifests.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-midbrain-sc"]
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with plates.json: the slug surf-interpeduncular-fossa is labelled on plate-midbrain-ic (lvl-midbrain-ic) while the record claims only lvl-midbrain-sc. The fossa is a ventral midline surface feature of the whole midbrain and is present at the inferior-colliculus level.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lvl-midbrain-ic to surf-interpeduncular-fossa.levels.
findings.notes: Cross-file: T5 owns the plate manifests.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-pons-rostral", "lvl-midbrain-ic", "lvl-midbrain-sc"]
findings.expected: either the level set extended caudally to lvl-pons-middle, or the committed mesh extended caudally — the two artifacts cannot both be right
findings.basis: Internal contradiction: plate-pons-middle (lvl-pons-middle, y = -8) labels nuc-mesencephalic-v and tract-mesencephalic-v, but both records' levels start at lvl-pons-rostral (y = +2) and the committed nuc-mesencephalic-v.glb occupies y 1.9..14.3 — 10 au rostral of the plate that shows it. Anatomically the mesencephalic trigeminal nucleus does begin at the level of the motor trigeminal nucleus in the mid-pons (Blumenfeld/Patten mid-pons plate), so the more likely defect is the caudal end of the frozen mesh, which is out of scope for this run.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not move the marker. Either add lvl-pons-middle to both records' levels (accepting that the frozen mesh does not reach it) or delete the two labels from plate-pons-middle; record the choice in CORRECTIONS.md, because a mesh change is out of scope.
findings.notes: Deliberately filed as suspect, not wrong: the auditor cannot decide between the record and the plate here, and the mesh cannot be moved in this run.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-olivary", "lvl-pontomedullary", "lvl-pons-caudal", "lvl-pons-middle", "lvl-pons-rostral"]
findings.expected: either the level set extended rostrally to lvl-midbrain-ic, or the label removed from plate-midbrain-ic
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with plates.json: plate-midbrain-ic (lvl-midbrain-ic, y = 8) labels ctx-cerebellum, but the record's levels stop at lvl-pons-rostral (y = +2) and its marker (y = -22 with a 14 au y-radius) reaches only y = -8. Anatomically the superior vermis does reach the collicular level (the tentorium sits at the colliculi), so the record's own rostral extent — a 14 au y-radius at y = -22 — is the more likely thing to be short.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lvl-midbrain-ic to ctx-cerebellum.levels, or remove the ctx-cerebellum label from plate-midbrain-ic; if the cerebellum's rostral extent is to be corrected, that is a size3d/origin3d change on this record (it owns no mesh) and must be declared.
findings.notes: Cross-file: T5 owns the plate manifests.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-olivary", "lvl-pontomedullary"]
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own committed mesh plus textbook anatomy: nuc-area-postrema.glb occupies y -32.8..-30.3 (2.5 au tall), so the lvl-pontomedullary anchor at y = -24 lies 6.3 au rostral of the structure's own rostral pole. The area postrema is a small circumventricular organ at the obex (this atlas's own surf-obex landmark is at y = -35 and its fourth-ventricle mesh ends at y = -31.6), and the obex is 11 au caudal of the pontomedullary junction; the organ cannot be present at lvl-pontomedullary.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop lvl-pontomedullary from nuc-area-postrema.levels. (Its own plate, plate-olivary, is the correct one and plate-pontomedullary does not exist.)
findings.notes: Effect is limited to the InfoPanel level chips, since the record's marker position does not follow levels.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-sensory-decuss", "lvl-olivary"]
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own committed mesh plus textbook anatomy: nuc-dmv.glb occupies y -33.4..-26.4, so lvl-sensory-decuss (y = -42) is 8.6 au caudal of the nucleus's own caudal pole and of the obex itself (surf-obex y = -35; the fourth-ventricle mesh ends at -31.6). The dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus lies under the vagal trigone of the OPEN medulla and does not extend into the closed medulla at the level of the sensory decussation. The record also omits lvl-pontomedullary, which its own mesh approaches (top -26.4 vs the anchor at -24).
findings.suggestedFix: Replace lvl-sensory-decuss with lvl-pontomedullary in nuc-dmv.levels; if the atlas wants to keep the label on plate-sensory-decuss, that plate carries a second, independent defect (T5).
findings.notes: Cross-file: plates.json labels nuc-dmv on plate-sensory-decuss, which is the artifact that agrees with the wrong level rather than with the mesh.

findings.field: levels vs own committed mesh bbox
findings.claimed: level sets reaching 4.4-12.8 au beyond the record's own frozen mesh (nuc-ambiguus 12.2 below/-10.5 above, nuc-vestibular-inferior +4.4/-5.8, nuc-vestibular-medial -15.9, nuc-vestibular-superior +6.3, nuc-hypoglossal -4.6/+6.9, nuc-nucleus-gracilis +7.4, nuc-nucleus-cuneatus +6.8, nuc-inferior-olive-principal +5.9, nuc-inferior-olive-medial +6.7, nuc-locus-coeruleus +4.7, nuc-trigeminal-motor +7.7, nuc-principal-sensory-v +7.7, nuc-spinal-trigeminal +12.8, nuc-dentate +11.3, nuc-interposed +12.3, nuc-fastigial +12.5)
findings.expected: either the level sets trimmed, or the meshes extended — the two cannot both be correct
findings.basis: Measured gap between each record's level-anchor y range and its own committed mesh y range. For several of these (nuc-ambiguus, nuc-vestibular-inferior, nuc-vestibular-medial, nuc-hypoglossal, nuc-spinal-trigeminal, the three deep cerebellar nuclei) standard anatomy supports the LEVEL SET, not the mesh — the nucleus ambiguus is a long column reaching the lower medulla, the spinal trigeminal nucleus spans mid-pons to C2, and the deep nuclei sit at the level of the mid-pons — so these look like short meshes, and moving a mesh is out of scope for this run (verify:anatomy is frozen). For the others the level set may itself over-claim, but this auditor cannot settle per record which artifact is wrong without a mesh move.
findings.suggestedFix: No fix proposed. Filed as an open question: the integrator should NOT trim level sets on the strength of a mesh that may itself be short (that would be a false correction); the two decidable cases in this family are filed separately as brainstem-012 (nuc-area-postrema) and brainstem-013 (nuc-dmv).
findings.notes: Deliberately a single pattern finding rather than 16 look-alike findings, so the ledger does not imply 16 independent defects. Reachable per-record numbers are in the notes list above.

findings.claimed: midline
findings.expected: paired (with the record noting that the midline central caudal subnucleus is the unpaired part)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own text: its function says 'arranged as paired subnuclei plus a single midline central caudal (levator) column' and 'Each subnucleus supplies contralateral target muscles except the superior rectus', and its clinical entry describes an IPSILATERAL third-nerve palsy — all of which require a paired nucleus. Laterality 'midline' also contradicts the atlas's own mechanical convention (midline = |x| < 1 au on a structure that is not paired) only semantically — but the semantic assignment is the audited question.
findings.suggestedFix: Change laterality to 'paired' with a note in `notes`/function that the central caudal subnucleus is unpaired; CAUTION: the committed nuc-oculomotor.glb is a single paramedian blob (x -2.1..0.7), so flipping the flag makes the renderer mirror that one blob into two copies offset by about 1.4 au. If the integrator judges that visual artefact worse than the semantic error, keep 'midline' and document the exception in CORRECTIONS.md instead.
findings.notes: Same convention question for nuc-edinger-westphal, nuc-trochlear and nuc-hypoglossal — filed separately so the integrator can decide them together.

findings.claimed: midline
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own text: 'its fibers curve dorsally around the cerebral aqueduct, decussate completely in the superior medullary velum' and the clinical entries describe a unilateral (one superior oblique) palsy. The trochlear nucleus is a paired nucleus (FMA: nucleus nervi trochlearis, right/left); its placement at x = 0 matches the atlas's single-blob mesh (x -1.1..0.0), not the anatomy.
findings.suggestedFix: Change laterality to 'paired' or document the single-blob convention; see the rendering caveat in brainstem-015.
findings.notes: Position is otherwise verified correct — see brainstem-042.

findings.claimed: midline
findings.basis: The Edinger-Westphal nucleus is a paired preganglionic nucleus (each side drives the ipsilateral ciliary ganglion), and the record's own connections say the pretectal input is bilateral, which is exactly what makes the light reflex consensual. A midline value is defensible only as the atlas's single-blob mesh convention: nuc-edinger-westphal.glb spans x -1.5..-0.3, i.e. entirely on one side of the midline, which is itself inconsistent with laterality 'midline'.
findings.suggestedFix: Change laterality to 'paired' (the mesh is one-sided already, so the mirror would draw the missing side) or document the exception; see brainstem-015 for the rendering caveat.
findings.notes: The one-sided mesh makes this the strongest case of the four midline CN nuclei for flipping the flag.

findings.claimed: midline
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own clinical text: 'Nuclear or rootlet destruction wastes the IPSILATERAL tongue' and 'Bilateral nuclear or rootlet lesions ... leave a tongue that can neither be protruded nor moved' — a statement that only makes sense for two separate nuclei. The two hypoglossal nuclei are separated by the midline raphe; the atlas's committed mesh spans x -1.1..1.0 (a single blob across the midline).
findings.suggestedFix: Change laterality to 'paired', or keep 'midline' and document that the two paramedian nuclei are drawn as one blob; see brainstem-015 for the rendering caveat.
findings.notes: Position itself verified correct — see brainstem-045.

findings.claimed: paired
findings.expected: midline (a single midline circumventricular organ at the obex)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own committed mesh: nuc-area-postrema.glb spans x -2.3..+2.3 as ONE blob crossing the midline, and the record's origin is x = 1.2 — i.e. the geometry is a midline structure while the field says one side. Terminologia Anatomica/FMA list the area postrema as a single (unpaired) structure; the record's own function text ('Paired circumventricular organ flanking the obex') is the only artifact calling it paired.
findings.suggestedFix: Set laterality to 'midline' and consider rewording 'Paired ... organ flanking the obex' to 'midline circumventricular organ at the obex'; the marker's x can stay at 1.2 or be zeroed, since a midline record is not mirrored.
findings.notes: Low impact (the paired mirror draws the same blob twice, overlapping), which is why this is minor.

findings.claimed: midline
findings.expected: either 'paired' with an explicit hemispheres record, or an explicit statement that the midline value is a deliberate single-envelope convention
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own name and contextNote (plan D4): the record is called 'Cerebellar hemispheres and vermis (context)' and its contextNote says the envelope is 'two hemispheres plus vermis bar', yet laterality is 'midline' and the taxonomy row is midline. A structure whose own description contains LATERAL hemispheres cannot be midline-only in the atlas's laterality semantics (midline = |x| < 1 au, paired = one side mirrored).
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the envelope as the renderable body, but make the semantics honest: either document in `notes`/contextNote that ctx-cerebellum is an intentionally unpaired midline envelope spanning both hemispheres (x-radius 10 au), or add a paired `surf-cerebellar-hemisphere-l` record so the lateralized hemisphere has a home. Either way, state the disposition in CORRECTIONS.md.
findings.notes: This is the architect's D4, verified here against the record text and the taxonomy row.

findings.claimed: region 'cerebellum' but authored inside src/data/structures/medulla.json, together with nuc-dentate, nuc-interposed, nuc-fastigial and surf-vermis
findings.expected: region/subdivision values are all correct and consistent with taxonomy.json; only the file placement is unusual, so either document it or move the five records to their own cerebellum file
findings.basis: Census checked in this audit: all five cerebellum records carry region 'cerebellum' and subdivisions 'Cerebellar context' / 'Deep cerebellar nuclei' / 'Surface landmarks', and taxonomy.json agrees row for row (5 cerebellum rows). File placement is not a rendered field, so nothing user-visible is wrong; this is the architect's D3, and the honest verdict is 'suspect', not 'wrong'.
findings.suggestedFix: No data change required. If the integrator wants a cleaner tree, the five records can move to src/data/structures/cerebellum.json without touching a single field (the loader walks src/data/structures/*.json). Otherwise record the disposition as 'rejected — file placement is not a rendered field'.
findings.notes: Affected ids: ctx-cerebellum, nuc-dentate, nuc-interposed, nuc-fastigial, surf-vermis.

findings.claimed: pons
findings.expected: medulla (or a documented hindbrain-level assignment for the whole vestibular complex)
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own levels and clinical text: its levels include lvl-olivary (y = -34, mid-medulla) and its clinical entry is about 'lesions at the caudal medulla or craniocervical junction — a dorsal PICA-territory infarct ... a Chiari malformation'. The inferior (descending) vestibular nucleus is a medullary nucleus in the standard figures (Blumenfeld's medulla plates, Nolte); the atlas files it — and the whole vestibular complex — under region 'pons', which is what the area toggle and the tree group on.
findings.suggestedFix: Set nuc-vestibular-inferior.region to 'medulla' (taxonomy row too), or keep 'pons' for the complex and add a one-line rationale in CORRECTIONS.md noting that the inferior vestibular nucleus is a medullary structure grouped with the pontine vestibular complex.
findings.notes: Only the inferior nucleus is at issue — the superior, medial and lateral nuclei are legitimately pontine (the medial one spans both); the region field drives the area filter, not the 3D position.

findings.claimed: medulla
findings.expected: either a documented hindbrain/cavity placement, or the region of the level where the record's own bulk sits
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own levels and mesh: its levels are lvl-pons-rostral, lvl-pons-middle, lvl-pons-caudal, lvl-pontomedullary, lvl-olivary (three of five purely pontine) and its committed GLB spans y -31.6..+4.5, i.e. the whole pons plus the upper medulla. Under region 'medulla' the fourth ventricle is shown by the medullary area toggle and hidden by the pontine one, although most of its geometry is pontine.
findings.suggestedFix: No field change is strictly required — the atlas has no hindbrain/cavity region — but record the disposition: either leave 'medulla' and document that the fourth ventricle is filed with the medulla as the caudal hindbrain area, or move it to the region of its centroid (pons).
findings.notes: Low impact: the record is a ventricle, not a nucleus, and is not part of any syndrome card.

findings.claimed: Tectum
findings.expected: Tegmentum (or a 'Pretectum' subdivision of its own)
findings.basis: Nomenclature: the tectum (lamina tecti) is the collicular plate — the two superior and two inferior colliculi with their laminae. The pretectal area/nuclei lie ROSTRAL to the superior colliculus at the diencephalic-midbrain junction and are not part of the tectum; Terminologia Anatomica lists the pretectal nuclei separately from the colliculi. In this atlas 'Tectum' otherwise contains exactly the two colliculus records, so the pretectal area is the odd one out.
findings.suggestedFix: Change nuc-pretectal.subdivision to 'Tegmentum' (and the taxonomy row with it) or introduce a 'Pretectum' subdivision; the choice also affects the group the record appears under in the tree.
findings.notes: The record's own level (lvl-post-comm) and mesh (y 16.0..18.5) already place it rostral to the colliculi, so the grouping contradicts the geometry it ships with.

findings.claimed: Cranial nerve nuclei
findings.expected: a tract subdivision — 'Cranial nerve tracts' or the existing 'Tegmentum'
findings.basis: Nomenclature/taxonomy: the record is kind 'tract' (the descending spinal tract of CN V), but it is filed under the subdivision 'Cranial nerve nuclei' — a subdivision whose own label excludes it. The same pattern occurs once more in this audit: tract-mesencephalic-v (midbrain.json) is also a tract under 'Cranial nerve nuclei'.
findings.suggestedFix: Either rename the subdivision to 'Cranial nerve nuclei and tracts' (one taxonomy edit fixes both records) or move the two tract records to 'Tegmentum'; do not split them, or the CN V nuclei and their tracts end up in different tree groups.
findings.notes: Affected ids: tract-spinal-trigeminal (medulla.json), tract-mesencephalic-v (midbrain.json). Purely a grouping label; no fact about the tract is wrong.

findings.claimed: also relays visual reflexes such as the pupillary light reflex through its rostral pretectal neighbors
findings.expected: the pupillary light reflex is relayed by the pretectum itself (retina -> brachium of the superior colliculus -> pretectum -> bilateral Edinger-Westphal); the superior colliculus is not a station of that reflex
findings.basis: Textbook: Blumenfeld's pupillary-control chapter (a ref the record itself cites) puts the light-reflex relay in the pretectal area; the retinotectal fibres that reach the superior colliculus serve orienting, not the pupillary arc. The record's own pretectal record (nuc-pretectal) assigns the reflex correctly to the pretectum, so the two records disagree about which structure relays it.
findings.suggestedFix: Reword to 'its rostral pretectal neighbours relay the pupillary light reflex, while the colliculus itself drives orienting saccades and eye-head turning'.
findings.notes: The rest of the record (retinotopy, multisensory map, nigral gating, tectospinal decussation) was checked and is correct.

findings.claimed: ["Dentate nucleus", "Interposed nuclei (emboliform and globose)"]
findings.expected: add the anterior (ventral) spinocerebellar tract — the one cerebellar AFFERENT that enters through the superior cerebellar peduncle
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with another authored record: the atlas's own tract-anterior-spinocerebellar says its target is 'Cerebellar cortex ... via the superior cerebellar peduncle' with a double crossing 'then recrossing within the superior cerebellar peduncle decussation at the caudal midbrain'. It was also checked against the atlas's conventions: afferent = where the fibres come from (tract-crus-cerebri: afferent = internal capsule; tract-icp: afferent = the olivary/cuneate/spinocerebellar sources), so the omission is a content gap, not a direction error.
findings.suggestedFix: Add 'Anterior (ventral) spinocerebellar tract (tract-anterior-spinocerebellar) — the uncrossed-again afferent of the peduncle' to tract-scp.connections.afferent and soften 'Principal efferent peduncle of the cerebellum' to 'principal (but not sole) efferent peduncle'.
findings.notes: Direction of every other SCP claim was verified: the dentatothalamic fibres cross in the decussation and the double-cross is what makes SCP lesions ipsilateral-ataxic (see brainstem-057).

findings.claimed: second-order relay ... for large-fiber discriminative touch, pressure and dental pulp sensation
findings.expected: discriminative touch, pressure and periodontal/dental mechanical sensation; pulpal NOCICEPTION belongs to the spinal trigeminal complex
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own clinical entry ('blunt ipsilateral discriminative touch over the face while pain-temperature (spinal trigeminal complex) is spared or affected separately') plus textbook anatomy: the dental pulp is supplied almost exclusively by A-delta and C nociceptors that terminate in the spinal trigeminal nucleus (pars oralis/caudalis), not in the principal sensory nucleus.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace 'and dental pulp sensation' with 'and periodontal mechanoreception' (or delete it); the atlas's own mesencephalic-V record already carries jaw/periodontal proprioception, so no new claim is needed.
findings.notes: The record's efferent list (ventral trigeminothalamic to contralateral VPM plus the small ipsilateral dorsal trigeminothalamic stream) was checked and is the standard textbook arrangement.

findings.claimed: primary afferents of the fasciculus gracilis terminate in tonotopically leg-arranged columns
findings.basis: Nomenclature plus self-contradiction: 'tonotopic' is the auditory term for frequency mapping and is meaningless for the dorsal column nuclei; the same clause already says 'leg-arranged', which is a somatotopic statement. The atlas uses 'tonotopic' correctly elsewhere (nuc-inferior-colliculus, tract-lateral-lemniscus), so this is a single word-level error, not a convention.
findings.suggestedFix: Change 'tonotopically leg-arranged columns' to 'somatotopically organised (leg-arranged) columns'.
findings.notes: Everything else in this record (first synapse of the DCML for the lower body, internal arcuate output, gracile tubercle) was verified correct.

findings.claimed: the medial accessory olive loses its climbing-fibre target and undergoes trans-synaptic hypertrophy
findings.expected: the olive loses its rubro-olivary INPUT (central tegmental tract from the contralateral red nucleus) and undergoes trans-synaptic degeneration/hypertrophy; its climbing fibres are its OUTPUT to the vermis, not its target
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own efferent field ('Climbing fibers to the vermis and vestibulocerebellum via tract-icp') and with textbook anatomy (Blumenfeld, Cerebellum; the Guillain-Mollaret triangle is dentate -> SCP -> contralateral red nucleus -> central tegmental tract -> ipsilateral inferior olive). Hypertrophic olivary degeneration is described in the inferior olivary nucleus — classically the principal olive — after its afferent is interrupted.
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite as '... loses its rubro-olivary input and undergoes trans-synaptic hypertrophy, while its climbing-fibre output to the vermis fails', and consider attributing the imaging finding to the olivary complex (or the principal olive) rather than to the medial accessory nucleus alone.
findings.notes: The sibling record nuc-inferior-olive-principal describes hypertrophic olivary degeneration correctly; only this record's mechanism sentence is inverted.

findings.claimed: Unilateral ambiguityus failure droops the ipsilateral palate ...
findings.expected: Unilateral ambiguus failure droops the ipsilateral palate ...
findings.basis: Nomenclature: 'ambiguityus' is a misspelling of the structure's own name (nucleus ambiguus) in a user-visible clinical string. The clinical content of the sentence is correct (the ipsilateral palate droops; the uvula then deviates away from the lesion, as the CN X nerve course states).
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the spelling to 'ambiguus'.
findings.notes: Only occurrence of this string in the atlas; purely a text fix, no geometry or claim change.

findings.claimed: ["Auditory nerve afferents (high-frequency fibers)", "Somatosensory and vestibular modulatory inputs"]
findings.expected: auditory-nerve afferents across the tonotopic range (the nucleus is tonotopically organised, high frequencies dorsally), not only high-frequency fibres
findings.basis: Textbook: the dorsal cochlear nucleus receives the ascending branch of the cochlear nerve from all frequency regions of the cochlea; only its internal tonotopic gradient puts high frequencies dorsally. The atlas's own function text for this record already implies a full-range input ('integrate auditory input with somatosensory and vestibular modulation' and 'spectral-shape cues'), so the afferent line narrows it incorrectly.
findings.suggestedFix: Reword to 'Auditory nerve afferents (full tonotopic range; the nucleus maps high frequencies dorsally)'.
findings.notes: Low severity: it is an afferent-list description, not a claim about the nucleus's role, and no clinical statement depends on it.

findings.claimed: bilateral dentate disease (Ceroid-lipofuscinosis, metronomic injury) disturbs movement timing
findings.expected: name an entity that exists — e.g. neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (Batten disease) and metronidazole/chemotherapy-related or radiation-induced cerebellar toxicity
findings.basis: Nomenclature/knowledge (labelled as such): 'metronomic injury' is not a recognised clinical entity; the adjacent causes in the atlas's own style would be metronidazole-induced cerebellar syndrome (which does affect the dentate nucleus) or posterior-fossa radiation. 'Ceroid-lipofuscinosis' is acceptable but the standard name is neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace 'metronomic injury' with the intended entity (metronidazole toxicity / radiation injury) or delete the parenthetical, and write 'neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (Batten disease)'.
findings.notes: Filed as suspect rather than wrong because the auditor cannot know which entity the author meant; the rest of the record (Purkinje input, dentatothalamic output, ipsilateral signs, Guillain-Mollaret link) is correct.

findings.claimed: Bilateral paramedian damage of the upper brainstem reticular core ... abolishes arousal while sparing sleep-wake behavioral cycling capacity of the cortex — the classic brainstem basis of coma.
findings.expected: bilateral damage to the paramedian reticular core of the upper brainstem/pons removes the ascending arousal input to an otherwise intact cortex and produces coma
findings.basis: Internal contradiction inside the sentence: if arousal is abolished, the cortex cannot be 'spared' a sleep-wake cycling capacity — the clause as written asserts that cortical sleep-wake cycling survives coma, which is the opposite of the intended point (that the CORTEX is intact and the arousal input is lost).
findings.suggestedFix: Reword to '... abolishes arousal while the cortex itself is structurally spared — the classic brainstem (ARAS) basis of coma'.
findings.notes: Wording defect in an otherwise correct entry; no localizing claim changes.

findings.claimed: then run the longest intracranial subarachnoid course of any cranial nerve up the clival dura
findings.expected: the longest cisternal/subarachnoid course in the posterior fossa; the 'longest intracranial course' superlative is claimed by surf-cn4-exit for the trochlear nerve in this same atlas
findings.basis: Internal contradiction between two authored records: surf-cn4-exit (midbrain.json) says the trochlear nerve has 'the longest intracranial subarachnoid course of any cranial nerve' and surf-cn6-exit (pons.json) claims the same superlative for the abducens. At most one can hold it. The classical teaching separates them — CN IV the longest (and thinnest) intracranial course, CN VI the longest cisternal course along the clivus — but this auditor will not award the superlative to one record on that basis alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Disambiguate the two sentences: give CN IV 'the longest intracranial course of any cranial nerve (and the thinnest)' and CN VI 'the longest cisternal/subarachnoid course in the posterior fossa, ascending the clivus to Dorello's canal'.
findings.notes: Both records are otherwise correct about the anatomy of their own nerve; only the shared superlative is at issue.

findings.claimed: ["gigantocellular reticular nucleus", "central/medial reticular nuclei of the medulla"]
findings.expected: the record's own name is 'Medullary reticular formation'; the gigantocellular and central/medial reticular nuclei are its SUBDIVISIONS, not synonyms of the whole
findings.basis: Nomenclature (Terminologia Anatomica / Nolte): the gigantocellular reticular nucleus (nucleus reticularis gigantocellularis) is one named nucleus within the medullary reticular formation, alongside the ventral, dorsal, central and lateral reticular nuclei. Presenting it as a synonym makes the atlas's labels non-interchangeable when they are not.
findings.suggestedFix: Reword the synonyms to 'medullary reticular nuclei (gigantocellular, central, ventral and dorsal) — the record covers the formation as a whole' or split the gigantocellular nucleus into its own record if the atlas wants a 1:1 name/id mapping.
findings.notes: Compare nuc-pprf, whose taxonomy row already uses `parent: nuc-pontine-reticular` — the same relation stated correctly.

findings.claimed: the olivary complex is authored as two records: nuc-inferior-olive-principal and nuc-inferior-olive-medial
findings.expected: the olivary complex also contains the dorsal accessory olivary nucleus (nucleus olivaris accessorius posterior), which is a named part of the Guillain-Mollaret circuitry
findings.basis: Nomenclature (Terminologia Anatomica/FMA): the inferior olivary complex comprises the principal olive, the medial accessory olive and the dorsal accessory olive (plus the dorsal cap). The atlas authors two of the three; the dorsal accessory olive is absent from taxonomy.json as well as from the structures files (checked by id and by name across src/data).
findings.suggestedFix: Either add nuc-inferior-olive-dorsal (registry row first, then a record with origin3d/size3d modelled on its two siblings) or record the omission as an accepted scope limit — it is a coverage gap, not a false claim.
findings.notes: Coverage finding: no existing field of this record is incorrect; the row is filed against the closest owning record so the ledger can disposition it.

findings.claimed: only the dorsal (rostral) raphe nucleus is authored; the raphe magnus, pallidus and obscurus appear only as prose
findings.expected: at least nucleus raphe magnus, which is the output stage of the PAG descending analgesia pathway named in nuc-pag and in this record
findings.basis: Internal contradiction of a weak kind: nuc-pag.connections.efferent says 'Nucleus raphe magnus and medullary reticular formation (descending analgesia)' and nuc-dorsal-raphe says 'Nucleus raphe magnus (descending pain control)', but no record and no taxonomy row carries that structure, so the medullary raphe group — one of the brief's explicit checklist items — has no home in the atlas.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nuc-raphe-magnus (and optionally pallidus/obscurus) with registry rows, or record the gap as an accepted scope limit; the prose references are correctly named either way.
findings.notes: Coverage finding, filed against the nearest raphe record.

findings.claimed: the rostral interstitial nucleus of the MLF (riMLF) and the interstitial nucleus of Cajal (INC) are named as afferents of nuc-oculomotor and nuc-trochlear and in the clinical text of nuc-vestibular-superior, but neither has a record or a taxonomy row
findings.expected: either records for the two vertical-gaze/ocular-tilt nuclei, or an explicit note that they are prose-only references
findings.basis: Checked across src/data: 'riMLF', 'rostral interstitial' and 'Cajal' resolve to no id in structures/, tracts.json or taxonomy.json, while four brainstem records depend on them (nuc-oculomotor afferent 'Rostral interstitial nucleus of the MLF and interstitial nucleus of Cajal (vertical gaze holding)', nuc-trochlear afferent, nuc-vestibular-superior clinical, nuc-edinger-westphal's near-response context). Naming WHERE THEY ARE USED is correct — this is a coverage gap, and the brief lists riMLF/INC/Cajal as checklist items.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the two records (registry rows first) or record the omission; do not silently retitle the existing prose, which is accurate as written.
findings.notes: Coverage finding, filed against the record that depends on them most.

findings.claimed: the atlas's brainstem clinical surface covers Weber, Benedikt, Claude, Nothnagel, Parinaud, Millard-Gubler, Foville, Wallenberg, Dejerine, hemimedullary, locked-in, one-and-a-half, INO and central Horner
findings.expected: Jackson syndrome (ipsilateral CN XII palsy with contralateral hemiplegia) and Raymond-Cestan syndrome (paramedian pontine tegmental syndrome) are missing from BOTH the syndrome cards and the records although the dispatch brief lists them
findings.basis: Exhaustive text search over src/data for 'Jackson' (hits only in telencephalon seizure/march entries), 'Raymond' (no hits) and 'Cestan' (no hits). The medial medullary card (syn-medial-medullary, eponym 'Dejerine (anterior bulbar) syndrome') already describes the exact Jackson pattern, so the pattern is covered under another eponym; the pontine Raymond-Cestan pattern (contralateral hemiplegia + ataxia, sometimes with INO and facial palsy) has no card at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add 'Jackson syndrome' as an alias of syn-medial-medullary (cheapest, and factually right) and add a Raymond-Cestan card, or record both as deliberate scope limits. Cross-file: syndrome cards belong to T6 audit-syndromes — this row is filed from the brainstem side so the gap is not lost between the two auditors.
findings.notes: Coverage finding; no existing record states anything false.

findings.basis: Checked against the committed meshes: nuc-oculomotor.glb y 12.6..15.4, z -5.4..-2.2 lies ventral to nuc-pag.glb (z -7.9..-4.1, the periaqueductal ring) and ventral to the aqueduct itself, and the marker is dorso-medial to the MLF at the same level (tract-mlf waypoint [1.5,14,-3.5]). This is the brief's exemplar 'oculomotor nucleus ventral to the PAG and dorsal to the MLF' — verified in the committed geometry.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: In this frame dorsoventral position is carried by z (dorsal negative), which is why 'ventral to the PAG' shows up as a larger z than the PAG's.

findings.basis: Committed mesh nuc-trochlear.glb y 6.9..9.0, z -6.4..-3.7 sits 5-6 au CAUDAL to nuc-oculomotor (y 12.6..15.4) and marginally dorsal (z -5 vs -4), at the inferior-colliculus level (lvl-midbrain-ic, y = 8) — the brief's exemplar, verified.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Laterality is filed separately as brainstem-016.

findings.basis: Committed mesh y -19.4..-16.4, x -3.0..3.0, z -5.1..-2.5: paramedian (x = 1.5), in the caudal pons (lvl-pons-caudal, y = -18) and DORSAL (z = -4) — directly under the facial colliculus landmark surf-facial-colliculus (z = -6, i.e. 2 au further dorsal, on the ventricular floor). The direction claims in the record were checked against tract-mlf: 'excitatory burst neurons of the ipsilateral PPRF' (nuc-pprf at [2,-18,-2], adjacent), 'internuclear axons crossing to ascend in the contralateral MLF toward nuc-oculomotor' — matches tract-mlf's own origin statement 'abducens internuclear neurons' and target 'oculomotor (medial rectus subnuclei)'.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: This is the brief's exemplar 'abducens in the caudal pons under the facial colliculus'.

findings.basis: Committed mesh y -20.7..-17.1, x -6.0..6.0, z -3.7..-0.3: the marker is 2.5 au LATERAL (x 4 vs 1.5) and 2 au VENTRAL (z -2 vs -4) to the abducens nucleus, which is the ventrolateral position of the caudal pons the brief asks for, and the record's function text describes the internal genu looping dorsomedially around that nucleus to make the facial colliculus.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Brief exemplar 'facial nucleus ventrolateral in the caudal pons with its fibres looping around the abducens'.

findings.basis: Committed mesh y -37.4..-30.9, x -1.1..1.0, z -5.3..-3.4. Against the MLF course at the same level (tract-mlf waypoint [1.2,-30,-3.5], next [1,-44,-2]) the hypoglossal marker is medial (x 0 vs 1.2) and dorsal (z -4 vs -3.5) — the brief's exemplar, verified; and the atlas's own surf-obex/vagal-trigone context (DMV at x 2, z -7) puts it medial to the dorsal vagal nucleus as expected.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Its levels (lvl-sensory-decuss .. lvl-pontomedullary) extend beyond the frozen mesh; that pattern is filed once as brainstem-014.

findings.basis: Committed mesh y -37.9..-29.9, x -7.0..7.0, z 1.0..5.0 contains the marker (0.23 au from the nearest olive surface vertex, inside by ray parity). The relations the brief asks for hold against its neighbours: lateral to the pyramid (tract-pyramid [3,-37,8]: olive x 5 > 3), dorsal to it (z 3 < 8), and ventral to the restiform body/ICP (tract-icp [7,-30,-3]: z 3 > -3). The medial accessory olive [2.5,-34,1] is correctly medial (x 2.5 < 5) and dorsal (z 1 < 3) to it.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Brief exemplar 'inferior olive ventrolateral between pyramid and restiform body'. Nomenclature of the two olivary records is otherwise correct (see brainstem-037 for the missing dorsal accessory olive).

findings.basis: The three deep nuclei are inside their own committed meshes and in the correct mediolateral order: fastigial [1.8,-22,-11.5] (mesh x -2.9..2.9) < interposed [4,-22,-11] (mesh x -5.3..5.4) < dentate [6,-22,-11] (mesh x -8.1..8.1); all three sit at z -11 to -11.5, DEEPER than the vermal surface landmark surf-vermis (z = -16.5) and dorsal to the fourth ventricle (origin z = -7.5) — the brief's 'vermis midline, hemispheres lateral, deep nuclei deep', verified for the nuclei.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Their level sets extend to lvl-pons-middle while the frozen meshes stop at y -24.7..-19.3 (part of the pattern filed as brainstem-014). 'Interposed (emboliform and globose)' is a legitimate lumping and both parts are named in the synonyms.

findings.basis: The vermis record is x = 0 with laterality 'midline' (correct for the midline strip) and lies at z = -16.5, i.e. dorsal to the deep nuclei (z -11..-11.5) and to the fourth ventricle (z -7.5), which is where the vermal cortex sits in the cerebellar roof. Its y span (marker ŷ -18 ± 12 au) matches its five pontine/medullary levels.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Laterality semantics of the enclosing ctx-cerebellum envelope is filed separately (brainstem-020).

findings.basis: The marker is 0.29 au from the dorsal surface of the committed medullary envelope ctx-medulla-surface.glb (ray parity inside), i.e. immediately under the ventricular floor at the vagal trigone, lateral to the hypoglossal nucleus (x 2 vs 0) and ventral to nuc-area-postrema (z -7 vs -8, the area postrema being the most dorsal structure of the group).
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Only its level set is wrong (brainstem-013).

findings.basis: Tested against the geometry: the point is OUTSIDE the inferior olive (2.04 au from its surface, parity 0/0/0), OUTSIDE the pyramid's own marker volume in the sense that matters (the pyramid marker [3,-37,8] has a z-radius of 1.8, so its dorsal surface is near z = 6.2) and inside the medullary envelope — i.e. in the pre-olivary sulcus between pyramid and olive, which is where the hypoglossal rootlets emerge. Its y (-32) is above the CN IX/X/XI row (-31 to -43) and its z (6.5) is between the pre-olivary and post-olivary values, exactly as the sulcus geography requires.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: This landmark is the reference that makes brainstem-004/-005 decidable: the IX and X landmarks at z = 4.5 fit neither sulcus.

findings.basis: 0.53 au from the surface of ctx-midbrain-surface.glb (parity inside) at the ventral midbrain, medial and ventral to the crus (tract-crus-cerebri [7,10,9]) and lateral to the midline — the sulcus of the oculomotor nerve on the medial cerebral peduncle. Its sibling surf-cn4-exit [1.5,7.5,-8] is 0.26 au from the same envelope on the DORSAL surface at the inferior-colliculus level, which is the only dorsal cranial-nerve exit.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Both midbrain exit landmarks are on their envelope surface; their pons and medulla siblings are the ones with defects (brainstem-003/-004/-005).

findings.basis: At the pontomedullary junction the point is 1.45 au OUTSIDE the committed pons envelope (parity 0/0/0), i.e. just ventral to the brainstem surface in the prepontine cistern, close to the midline (x 2.5) and far lateral to nothing else — the correct ventromedial exit position for CN VI, which is why the derived course in curves.ts leaves the pons ventrally and then ascends the clivus.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Function text is filed separately for the shared superlative (brainstem-035).

findings.basis: 0.15 au from the surface of the pons envelope (parity outside) — the cerebellopontine-angle corner in this frame — and 1.5 au ANTERIOR to its sibling surf-cn8-exit [6.8,-22,-4.5], which is the correct VII-in-front-of-VIII relation at the internal acoustic meatus. surf-cn8-exit itself is 1.25 au inside the envelope, within the smoothing tolerance of the sculpted envelope.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: The two landmarks are what the CN VII and CN VIII courses are anchored on (curves.ts waypoints 2 and 3).

findings.claimed: every record's region, subdivision and laterality
findings.basis: Mechanical comparison of all 80 records against the 248-row registry: 80/80 agree on region, subdivision and laterality, and every id in the three files resolves to a registry row (no 'awaiting authored record'). The semantic questions that remain (which value is RIGHT) are filed individually as brainstem-002x.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Registry-first rule of the plan holds: no brainstem record lacks a taxonomy row.

findings.claimed: 24 distinct id-shaped references (nuc-*, tract-*, ctx-*, surf-*) inside the 80 records
findings.expected: all of them resolve to a structure, tract or registry row
findings.basis: Extracted every token matching /(nuc|tract|ctx|surf|vent|nrv|vasc)-[a-z0-9-]+/ from the 80 records and looked each one up in structures/*.json + tracts.json + taxonomy.json: 0 dangling. (Name-only references such as 'nucleus raphe magnus' or 'interstitial nucleus of Cajal' are prose, not ids, and are covered by brainstem-038/039.)
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Reference integrity is therefore clean within the brainstem set; the defects found in this audit are content and geometry, not broken links.

findings.claimed: Benedikt = CN III palsy + contralateral tremor/choreoathetosis/ataxia; Claude = CN III palsy + prominent contralateral ataxia; Holmes/rubral tremor 2-4.5 Hz
findings.basis: Checked against the midbrain cards and the standard definitions: syn-benedikt (structures nuc-oculomotor, nuc-edinger-westphal, nuc-red-nucleus, tract-medial-lemniscus) and syn-claude (nuc-red-nucleus, nuc-oculomotor, nuc-dentate, tract-scp) agree with this record's own entries — same side of the CN III palsy (ipsilateral), same laterality of the movement disorder (contralateral), same vascular attribution (paramedian PCA perforators). Blood supply of the nucleus (paramedian PCA/basilar tip, SCA laterally) is the standard territory.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Nothnagel is not carried by any brainstem record, so its vascular attribution could not be cross-read from this file; it lives in syn-nothnagel (PCA collicular + SCA) and in the CN III nerve record, which claims ipsilateral ataxia PLUS contralateral hemianesthesia — a different content set from the syndrome card. That is a real inter-file inconsistency but both files belong to other auditors (T4/T6), so it is reported in the .md as a hand-off, not filed as a brainstem finding.

findings.claimed: unilateral PPRF lesion = ipsilateral conjugate gaze palsy with the eyes deviated away and no diplopia; PPRF + ipsilateral MLF = one-and-a-half syndrome with contralateral abduction as the only residual movement; Doll's-eye may still move the eyes
findings.basis: Laterality and residual-movement logic checked against tract-mlf and syn-one-and-a-half: a left-sided dorsal pontine lesion leaves abduction of the RIGHT eye as the single horizontal movement, which is what this record and the card both say; 'eyes deviated away from the lesion' and 'conjugacy preserved so no diplopia' are the textbook bedside signs; the oculocephalic bypass is correct because the VOR reaches the abducens nucleus without the PPRF (tract-mlf origin lists the vestibular nuclei).
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: PPRF position [2,-18,-2] is inside its own mesh and paramedian at the abducens level, and its taxonomy row carries parent: nuc-pontine-reticular — both correct.

findings.claimed: involvement of the descending hypothalamospinal fibres in the lateral reticular tegmentum yields ipsilateral ptosis and miosis as part of Wallenberg syndrome
findings.basis: Cross-read against syn-central-horner (structures tract-hypothalamospinal + nuc-medullary-reticular) and tract-hypothalamospinal (uncrossed, descends ipsilaterally through the lateral brainstem tegmentum to the C8-T2 ciliospinal centre): the deficit is ipsilateral, first-order, and the artery is PICA/vertebral — all three statements agree across the three artifacts. The record's other two clinical entries (central sleep apnoea, neurogenic hypertension from the rostral ventrolateral pressor area) are also correct for the lateral medullary syndrome.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Only its synonyms are imprecise (brainstem-036).

findings.claimed: subnucleus caudalis laminated like the dorsal horn with perioral fibres most rostral, so caudal/dorsal lesions numb the outer face, ear and scalp while sparing nose and mouth; tract and nucleus are clinically indistinguishable
findings.basis: The laminar/onion-skin statement matches the standard account and matches this record's sibling tract record (tract-spinal-trigeminal: 'V1 most ventral/rostral and V3 most dorsal/caudal'), and the crossed pattern (ipsilateral face, contralateral body) matches syn-lateral-medullary and the record's own PICA/vertebral attribution. Its afferent/efferent direction is correct (tract -> nucleus; nucleus -> ventral trigeminothalamic tract and reflex interneurons to facial/ambiguus).
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Its long level set (7 anchors) is anatomically right even though its frozen mesh is 12.8 au shorter (brainstem-014).

findings.claimed: unilateral pyramid lesion = contralateral hemiparesis with the face spared; Weber, Millard-Gubler and Dejerine as the crossed families; anterior spinal artery territory
findings.basis: Cross-read against syn-medial-medullary (Dejerine: contralateral hemiparesis + contralateral lemniscal loss + ipsilateral tongue), syn-millard-gubler and syn-weber, and against the arteries file: the medullary pyramid is anterior-spinal-artery territory, its lesion is pre-decussation, and the face sparing (separate corticobulbar crossing) is the standard discriminator from a capsular stroke. Its afferent line names tract-corticospinal-lateral exactly as the pons records do, which is the atlas's own convention for the descending bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Its decussation fraction (85-90 %) and the cruciate-paralysis entry in tract-pyramidal-decussation are also correct.

findings.claimed: dentate/interposed fibres decussate completely in the ventral midbrain tegmentum to the contralateral red nucleus and VL/VA thalamus; because cerebellar output double-crosses, lesions here cause ipsilateral limb ataxia
findings.basis: Direction and laterality checked against tract-scp-decussation (midline, [0,7,2], ventral tegmentum), nuc-red-nucleus (afferent 'contralateral dentate and interposed via the SCP decussation'), the SCA territory and syn-cerebellar ('signs are ipsilateral because cerebellar efferents cross twice'). The double-cross argument is the standard one.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: The one content gap (the anterior spinocerebellar afferent) is filed as brainstem-027.

findings.field: connections (direction of the cerebellar afferent gateway)
findings.claimed: afferent: inferior olivary complex (both records), cuneocerebellar fibres, posterior spinocerebellar tract, vestibular nuclei; efferent: cerebellar cortex
findings.basis: Direction is correct in the atlas's convention (afferent = source of the fibres) and matches tract-posterior-spinocerebellar ('join the inferior cerebellar peduncle in the upper medulla', uncrossed), nuc-nucleus-cuneatus ('cuneocerebellar fibers via the inferior cerebellar peduncle'), nuc-vestibular-superior/inferior and the olivary records' climbing-fibre output. Position [7,-30,-3] is dorsolateral to the olive and to the pyramid, which is where the restiform body lies.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Its Wallenberg-related clinical entries (ipsilateral ataxia from the restiform body, vestibular pseudo-neuritis with HINTS) are correct and match syn-lateral-medullary.

findings.basis: This is the surface record whose whole purpose is the abducens/facial-genu relation the brief asks about: it lies at x = 1.8 (same paramedian column as nuc-abducens at x = 1.5) and z = -6, i.e. 2 au DORSAL to the abducens nucleus (z = -4) and dorsal to the facial nucleus (z = -2) — on the fourth-ventricle floor over the nucleus, exactly as the internal genu of CN VII produces it. It is 0.64 au outside the pons envelope, consistent with a ventricular-floor bulge.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Its Foville clinical entry agrees with syn-foville (gaze palsy + ipsilateral LMN facial palsy, with the hemiplegia optional), so the eponym is used consistently across the two files.

findings.claimed: LMNs to the striated muscles of soft palate, pharynx and larynx through CN IX, CN X and the cranial root of CN XI; solitarius afferents complete the swallow and gag arcs
findings.basis: Matches the CN IX/X/XI nerve courses in curves.ts (stylopharyngeus via IX; palate/pharynx/larynx via X; laryngeal adductors via the cranial root of XI hitching onto the vagus), the nucleus solitarius record's efferent list (ambiguus for the swallow/gag motor arc) and syn-lateral-medullary (hoarseness, drooping palate, depressed gag). Position is inside its own mesh and within the reticular formation (1.81 au from the envelope surface).
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Its misspelling finding (brainstem-031) is a text fix only; its frozen mesh is shorter than its own level set (brainstem-014).

findings.claimed: efferent: vestibular and reticular nuclei via tract-icp, plus the contralateral VL/red-nucleus region via tract-scp
findings.basis: The fastigial nucleus's output leaves mainly through the uncinate fasciculus of the inferior cerebellar peduncle to the vestibular and reticular nuclei, with a smaller ascending component through the superior cerebellar peduncle — which is what the record says, and what ctx-cerebellum's own efferent line ('SCP — dentate/interposed/fastigial output') and syn-cerebellar assume. Its clinical entry (truncal/axial ataxia with relatively preserved limb coordination) matches surf-vermis and the vermal entries.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Median position (x 1.8, medialmost of the three nuclei) verified in brainstem-047.

findings.claimed: paired
findings.expected: paired is acceptable (the trapezoid body is conventionally drawn per side, with the decussation at the midline)
findings.basis: The record's own function text carries the crossing explicitly ('axons of ventral cochlear nucleus neurons cross here to reach the contralateral superior olivary complex'), which is what a laterality flag cannot express; the paired convention matches tract-trigeminothalamic-ventral and tract-corticospinal-lateral, whose decussations are likewise described in `decussation`/prose rather than in the flag. No internal contradiction found.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Recorded so the integrator does not 'fix' a flag that the atlas's convention does not use for midline crossings.

findings.claimed: subdivision 'Reticular formation', synonyms include 'mesencephalic reticular formation', 'pedunculopontine region (adjacent)'
findings.expected: unchanged — the cuneiform nucleus is a named part of the mesencephalic reticular formation, and the record correctly flags the pedunculopontine region as ADJACENT rather than identical
findings.basis: Checked for over-claim and found none of consequence: the function text says 'mesencephalic reticular formation of the dorsolateral tegmentum (with the adjacent pedunculopontine region forming the mesencephalic locomotor region)', which is the standard composition of the MLR, and its connections (PAG, hypothalamus, spinoreticular input, descending reticulospinal output, intralaminar arousal) are correct for the nucleus. Position [7,11,-4] is inside its own mesh (x -8.8..8.8, z -5.4..-2.6), dorsolateral at the collicular levels.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: The absent subcuneiform nucleus is a coverage matter noted in the .md, not a defect of this record (the record does not claim to cover it).

findings.claimed: tent-shaped midline CSF cavity between the dorsal pons and medulla in front and the cerebellum behind, continuous rostrally with the aqueduct and caudally with the central canal at the obex; outflow through Luschka and Magendie; floor carries the facial colliculus, hypoglossal trigone and vagal trigone
findings.basis: Every clause checked: the outflow foramina, the aqueduct/central-canal continuity at the obex (this atlas's own surf-obex at [0,-35,-8] and nuc-area-postrema just rostral to it), and the three floor landmarks all exist as records (surf-facial-colliculus, nuc-hypoglossal, nuc-dmv) and sit where the text says. Its committed mesh (y -31.6..+4.5) is consistent with the levels it claims.
findings.suggestedFix: none (verified)
findings.notes: Its region value is filed separately (brainstem-023).
